stem: A 55-year-old man with a history of end-stage renal disease due to polycystic kidney disease is scheduled to undergo living-donor kidney transplantation.  To harvest the donor kidney, a laparoscopic left nephrectomy is performed on the living donor.  During the procedure, the left kidney and proximal ureter are visualized, and a short segment of proximal ureter is harvested with its surrounding periureteric tissue preserved to maintain blood supply after transplantation.  Which of the following arteries normally supplies blood to this portion of the ureter?​‌​‌‌‌‌‌‌‌​‌‌‌‌‌​‌‌‌‌‌‌‌​‌‌‌‌‌​​‌​​​​​​​‌​‌‌​‌‌‌‌‌​‌​​‌‌‌​​​‌‌​​​​‌‌‌‌​​​‌‌‌‌‌‌‌‌​‌​‌‌‌​​​‌​‌​​‌‌‌‌​‌​​‌‌​‌‌‌‌​‌​​‌​​‌‌​​‌​‌‌​​​‌‌​‌​​​‌‌​​‌​‌​​‌‌‌‌‌‌​​‌‌‌​‌‌‌​‌‌​​‌‌‌​‌​​​​​​‌‌​​​‌‌​‌​​‌‌​‌​​‌‌​​​​​​‌​‌‌​​‌‌​​​​‌‌​​​‌​​​​‌‌‌​​​​‌​​‌‌​‌‌​​‌​​‌‌​​​​​‌​​​​‌​‌‌​​‌‌​‌​​‌‌​​​​‌‌​​​​​​‌​​‌‌​‌‌​‌‌​​​‌‌​​‌​‌​‌​‌‌‌​​​​‌‌‌‌​‌‌‌​‌‌​‌‌​​‌​​​​
explanation:
The blood supply to the proximal ureter comes from branches of the renal artery.  Supply to the distal ureter arises from branches of the internal iliac system, especially the superior vesical artery.  In between, the arterial supply to the ureter is anastomotic and highly variable, with possible afferent branches from the gonadal, common and internal iliac, and aortic arteries.

During a kidney transplant operation, the native kidneys are typically left in place, and the donor kidney is placed retroperitoneally in the right iliac fossa.  Blood supply is established by anastomosing the donor renal artery to the recipient's iliac artery, most commonly the external iliac artery.  A short, well-vascularized segment of the donor ureter is preserved and used to establish continuity from the collecting system of the kidney to the recipient's bladder.

Although the transplanted ureter continues to receive blood through branches of the donor renal artery, the most distal portion may be susceptible to ischemia because it no longer has its native pelvic collateral supply.  Distal ureteral ischemia is a recognized complication of renal transplant and can cause urine leakage, typically within the first 1-2 weeks following transplant.

(Choices A, B, and F)  Branches from the common iliac, internal iliac, and superior vesical arteries supply more distal segments of the ureter.  These segments are not typically retained in the transplanted specimen in order to prevent distal ureteral ischemia.

(Choice C)  The lumbar arteries arise directly from the aorta to supply the lumbar vertebrae and surrounding structures.

(Choice D)  The inferior phrenic arteries usually arise from the abdominal aorta and supply the diaphragm. They also give off branches to the superior portion of the adrenal glands.

Educational objective:The proximal ureter receives its blood supply from the renal artery. Circulation to the middle and distal portions of the ureter is variable and anastomotic; distal contributions arise from branches of the internal iliac system, including the superior vesical artery.​‌​‌‌‌‌‌‌‌​‌‌‌‌‌​‌‌‌‌‌‌‌​‌‌‌‌‌​​‌​​​​​​​‌​‌‌​‌‌‌‌‌​‌​​‌‌‌​​​‌‌​​​​‌‌‌‌​​​‌‌‌‌‌‌‌‌​‌​‌‌‌​​​‌​‌​​‌‌‌‌​‌​​‌‌​‌‌‌‌​‌​​‌​​‌‌​​‌​‌‌​​​‌‌​‌​​​‌‌​​‌​‌​​‌‌‌‌‌‌​​‌‌‌​‌‌‌​‌‌​​‌‌‌​‌​​​​​​‌‌​​​‌‌​‌​​‌‌​‌​​‌‌​​​​​​‌​‌‌​​‌‌​​​​‌‌​​​‌​​​​‌‌‌​​​​‌​​‌‌​‌‌​​‌​​‌‌​​​​​‌​​​​‌​‌‌​​‌‌​‌​​‌‌​​​​‌‌​​​​​​‌​​‌‌​‌‌​‌‌​​​‌‌​​‌​‌​‌​‌‌‌​​​​‌‌‌‌​‌‌‌​‌‌​‌‌​​‌​​​​
